features.name: dsatur_firstfit_scarcity
features.code:
import numpy as np


def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """DSATUR-style saturation, remaining-degree share, first-fit colour index, and scarcity of the blocked colour classes."""
    nc = np.asarray(neighbor_colors, dtype=float)
    k, c = nc.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 4))

    blocked = nc > 0                                   # (k, c) which used colours touch a candidate
    sat = blocked.sum(axis=1)                          # distinct neighbour colours

    adj = np.asarray(adjacency, dtype=float)
    rem_share = adj.sum(axis=1) / max(k - 1, 1)        # share of the uncoloured set adjacent to it

    if c == 0:
        return np.stack([np.zeros(k), rem_share, np.zeros(k), np.zeros(k)], axis=1)

    zero = nc == 0                                     # colours still free for this candidate
    first = np.argmax(zero, axis=1).astype(float)      # first free colour = colour it would get
    first = np.where(~zero.any(axis=1), float(c), first)

    sizes = np.asarray(color_sizes, dtype=float)[:c]
    scarcity = blocked @ (1.0 / (sizes + 1.0))         # blocked colours weighted by how rare the class is

    return np.stack(
        [
            sat / (c + 1.0),
            rem_share,
            first / (c + 1.0),
            scarcity / (c + 1.0),
        ],
        axis=1,
    )
features.measures: DSATUR-style saturation, remaining-degree share, first-fit colour index, and scarcity of the blocked colour classes.

features.name: forced_new_color_pressure
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Fraction of a candidate's uncoloured neighbours that would be forced to open a new colour if it took its smallest available colour."""
    neighbor_colors = np.asarray(neighbor_colors)
    k = neighbor_colors.shape[0]
    deg = np.asarray(degree, dtype=float)
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]
    if c == 0:
        # first decision: no colours used yet, fall back to plain degree
        m = deg.max()
        return deg / (m + 1e-9) if m > 0 else np.zeros(k)

    free = (neighbor_colors == 0)                 # (k, c) colours still available to each candidate
    has_free = free.any(axis=1)
    first_free = np.where(has_free, free.argmax(axis=1), 0)
    free_count = free.sum(axis=1)
    single = (free_count == 1)                    # neighbour has exactly one existing colour left

    share = free.T[first_free]                    # (k, k): share[i, j] = free[j, first_free[i]]
    mask = share & single[None, :] & has_free[:, None]
    adj_f = np.asarray(adjacency, dtype=float)
    forced = (adj_f * mask).sum(axis=1)           # neighbours pushed into opening a new colour

    colored = neighbor_colors.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    unc = np.maximum(deg - colored, 0.0)
    out = forced / (unc + 1.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
features.measures: Fraction of a candidate's uncoloured neighbours that would be forced to open a new colour if it took its smallest available colour.

features.name: saturation_uncoloured_degree_blocking
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours already touching it, fraction of its neighbours still uncoloured, and how many of those uncoloured neighbours could still take the colour it would itself take."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)

    # saturation: how many distinct colours already sit on its neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / max(c, 1)

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree: how much freedom is left in its local subgraph
    uncol = adjacency.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    # the colour this candidate would take: first zero column, else a new colour c
    avail = neighbor_colors == 0                      # (k, c)
    if c == 0:
        first = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.intp)            # no colours yet -> new colour 0
        avail_full = np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)
    else:
        any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
        avail_full = np.concatenate([avail, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)

    # lose[i, j] = True if colour that candidate i would take is still free for candidate j
    lose = avail_full[:, first].T.astype(float)
    impact = (adjacency.astype(float) * lose).sum(axis=1)
    impact_frac = impact / dmax

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, impact_frac])
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours already touching it, fraction of its neighbours still uncoloured, and how many of those uncoloured neighbours could still take the colour it would itself take.

features.name: dsatur_saturation_plus_degree

idea.hypothesis: Code Zero colours by index, so a vertex is often coloured after its neighbours have already consumed several colours; nothing steers the order toward the most constrained vertex. Saturation (number of distinct colours already present among coloured neighbours) is the classical fix: colour the vertex with the fewest remaining legal colours first, which stops a vertex arriving late with all colours blocked. Returning degree as a second column gives DSATUR its standard tie-break at the first decision (c=0, where saturation is constant) and lets the optimiser weigh degree separately.
idea.feature: Return two columns. c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]. col0: zeros if c==0, else (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1) / c  (fraction of used colours present at a coloured neighbour). col1: degree.astype(float) / max(1.0, float(degree.max())). Shape (k, 2).

features.measures: Two columns: fraction of used colours present at a coloured neighbour, and degree normalised by the maximum candidate degree.

features.name: one_step_forced_new_colour
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Negated fraction of the candidate's slack-holding uncoloured neighbours whose only remaining free colour is exactly the candidate's first-fit colour."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0 or c == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    zeros_mask = (neighbor_colors == 0)
    n_zero = zeros_mask.sum(axis=1)
    first_zero = zeros_mask.argmax(axis=1)          # 0 where n_zero == 0, masked below
    f = np.where(n_zero > 0, first_zero, c)         # first-fit colour (c = brand-new colour)

    adj = np.asarray(adjacency, dtype=bool)
    has_slack = (n_zero > 0).astype(float)

    # neighbours that still hold at least one free colour: the only ones a choice can constrain
    denom = adj.astype(float) @ has_slack

    forcings = (
        (n_zero == 1)[None, :]
        & (first_zero[None, :] == f[:, None])
        & adj
    )
    forced = forcings.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    return -forced / np.maximum(1.0, denom)

idea.hypothesis: The diagnostics show new colours opened very late (dense 98.6%, geometric 95% of the order) and singleton classes appearing. A candidate's first-fit colour f closes the last free colour of any uncoloured neighbour whose only zero column is f, forcing that neighbour to open a brand-new colour later. Scoring a candidate by how many neighbours it forces (negated) keeps the remaining graph unconstrained and should reduce forced new colours and the singletons they create.
idea.feature: c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]; return zeros(k) if c==0. Else: zeros_mask = (neighbor_colors == 0); n_zero = zeros_mask.sum(axis=1); first_zero = argmax(zeros_mask, axis=1); f = where(n_zero > 0, first_zero, c) (the first-fit colour). forced[i] = number of j with adjacency[i,j] and n_zero[j] == 1 and first_zero[j] == f[i], i.e. ((n_zero == 1)[None,:] & (first_zero[None,:] == f[:,None]) & adjacency).sum(axis=1). udeg = adjacency.sum(axis=1). Return -forced / maximum(1.0, udeg).

features.coder_note: The code computes, for each candidate, minus the number of its uncoloured neighbours that have exactly one free colour equal to the candidate's first-fit colour, divided by the candidate's uncoloured degree; with `c == 0` it returns zeros, as specified.
features.measures: Negated fraction of the candidate's slack-holding uncoloured neighbours whose only remaining free colour is exactly the candidate's first-fit colour.

features.name: fill_small_existing_class
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Prefer candidates whose first-fit colour is a small existing class, and penalise those that would open a new colour."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if c == 0:
        return np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

    zeros_mask = neighbor_colors == 0
    n_zero = zeros_mask.sum(axis=1)
    first_fit = np.where(n_zero > 0, np.argmax(zeros_mask, axis=1), c)

    n = k + color_sizes.sum()
    sizes = color_sizes / max(1.0, float(n))
    existing = n_zero > 0

    safe_first_fit = np.minimum(first_fit, c - 1)
    fill = np.where(existing, 1.0 - sizes[safe_first_fit], -1.0)
    return fill.astype(float)

idea.hypothesis: The champion's classes are badly unbalanced (dense smallest_class 1 vs ref 5, geometric 3 singletons vs ref 0) while the reference keeps classes even. Because the assigned colour is fixed by first-fit, the only lever is which candidate goes next: a candidate whose first-fit colour belongs to a small existing class grows that class and flattens the distribution, whereas a candidate that would open a new colour class starts a guaranteed singleton. Penalising new-colour openers and preferring small existing classes should raise smallest_class and cut singletons.
idea.feature: c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]; return zeros(k) if c==0. Else: zeros_mask = (neighbor_colors == 0); n_zero = zeros_mask.sum(axis=1); f = where(n_zero > 0, argmax(zeros_mask, axis=1), c). n = k + color_sizes.sum(); sizes = color_sizes / max(1.0, n). existing = n_zero > 0. fill = where(existing, 1.0 - sizes[minimum(f, c-1)], -1.0). Return fill (in [-1, 1)).

features.coder_note: The code computes, for each candidate, `1 - (size of the existing colour class it would join)/n` if first-fit assigns it an existing colour, otherwise `-1` for opening a new colour; I read “small existing class” as the class with the smallest size-valued term under the stated formula.
features.measures: Prefer candidates whose first-fit colour is a small existing class, and penalise those that would open a new colour.

features.name: second_order_saturation_pressure
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, its fraction of uncoloured neighbours, and the average colour-saturation of those uncoloured neighbours (second-order blocking pressure)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    cmax = max(c, 1)

    # first-order saturation: how many distinct colours already sit on its neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / cmax

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree: how much freedom is left in its local subgraph
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    # second-order pressure: average saturation among the candidate's uncoloured
    # neighbours -- a vertex hemmed in by already-constrained neighbours should be
    # coloured before its own first-order saturation catches up.
    nb_sat = adjf @ sat
    nb_sat_frac = nb_sat / np.maximum(uncol * cmax, 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, nb_sat_frac])
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, its fraction of uncoloured neighbours, and the average colour-saturation of those uncoloured neighbours (second-order blocking pressure).

features.name: first_fit_class_closure
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """For each candidate's first-fit colour class: how closed it is (few other uncoloured vertices can still take it), how full it becomes if the candidate joins it, and how many of its uncoloured neighbours could also take it; new-colour candidates score -1 throughout."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=float)
    if c == 0:
        return np.full((k, 3), -1.0, dtype=float)

    avail = neighbor_colors == 0                       # (k, c) colours still free for each candidate
    n_zero = avail.sum(axis=1)
    first_fit = np.where(n_zero > 0, avail.argmax(axis=1), c)
    existing = n_zero > 0

    # global: how many uncoloured candidates can still take each colour
    col_free = avail.sum(axis=0).astype(float)
    safe = np.where(existing, first_fit, 0)
    free_j = col_free[safe]                            # includes the candidate itself

    others = max(k - 1, 1)
    closure = 1.0 - np.maximum(free_j - 1.0, 0.0) / others

    # parent thread, changed: small/saturating class relative to its remaining demand
    sizes_j = color_sizes[safe].astype(float)
    completion = (sizes_j + 1.0) / (sizes_j + np.maximum(free_j, 1.0))

    # local: uncoloured neighbours that could also take the chosen colour
    neigh_can = adjacency.astype(float) @ avail.astype(float)   # (k, c)
    sel = neigh_can[np.arange(k), safe]
    uncol_deg = adjacency.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    local = sel / np.maximum(uncol_deg, 1.0)

    out = np.column_stack([closure, completion, local])
    out = np.where(existing[:, None], out, -1.0)
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0)
features.measures: For each candidate's first-fit colour class: how closed it is (few other uncoloured vertices can still take it), how full it becomes if the candidate joins it, and how many of its uncoloured neighbours could also take it; new-colour candidates score -1 throughout.

features.name: firstfit_colour_regret
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """How much more contested a candidate's first-fit colour is (neighbours sharing it) than the average of its other free colours, per uncoloured neighbour."""
    nc = np.asarray(neighbor_colors)
    k, c = nc.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    # one extra column standing for a fresh colour, always free for everyone
    if c > 0:
        free_existing = (nc == 0)
    else:
        free_existing = np.zeros((k, 0), dtype=bool)
    free_full = np.concatenate([free_existing, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)  # (k, c+1)

    adj = np.asarray(adjacency).astype(float)
    # comp[i, j] = number of uncoloured neighbours of i that could also take colour j
    comp = adj @ free_full.astype(float)                     # (k, c+1)

    target = free_full.argmax(axis=1)                        # first free colour (always exists)
    rows = np.arange(k)
    target_comp = comp[rows, target]

    # average competition over the candidate's *other* free colours
    nfree = free_full.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sum_free_comp = (comp * free_full).sum(axis=1)
    other_mean = (sum_free_comp - target_comp) / np.maximum(nfree - 1.0, 1.0)

    uncol_deg = adj.sum(axis=1)
    return (target_comp - other_mean) / np.maximum(uncol_deg, 1.0)
features.measures: How much more contested a candidate's first-fit colour is (neighbours sharing it) than the average of its other free colours, per uncoloured neighbour.

features.name: neighbour_saturation_and_two_hop_colour_reach
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Second-order colour structure: the mean saturation of a candidate's uncoloured neighbours, and the fraction of used colours reachable within two uncoloured hops (a colour on a neighbour, or on a neighbour of a neighbour)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0 or c == 0:
        return np.zeros((k, 2))
    # colours already sitting on each uncoloured vertex's coloured neighbours
    present = neighbor_colors > 0                       # (k, c) bool
    sat = present.sum(axis=1).astype(float)             # (k,)

    adj = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol_deg = adj.sum(axis=1)

    # how saturated are the uncoloured vertices next to me (smoothed DSATUR)
    nbr_sat = (adj @ sat) / np.maximum(uncol_deg, 1.0)

    # colours present at distance <= 2 through the uncoloured subgraph
    twohop = (adj @ present.astype(float)) > 0          # (k, c) bool
    reach = (present | twohop).sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    col1 = np.clip(nbr_sat / c, 0.0, 1.0)
    col2 = np.clip(reach / c, 0.0, 1.0)
    return np.column_stack([col1, col2])
features.measures: Second-order colour structure: the mean saturation of a candidate's uncoloured neighbours, and the fraction of used colours reachable within two uncoloured hops (a colour on a neighbour, or on a neighbour of a neighbour).

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: (1) share of its coloured neighbours that pile onto its single busiest colour class, and (2) how much of its degree touches the globally largest colour class."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0 or c == 0:
        return np.zeros((k, 2))
    nc = neighbor_colors.astype(float)

    # coloured neighbours = total neighbour-colour incidences
    colored = nc.sum(axis=1)
    max_local = nc.max(axis=1)
    concentration = np.where(colored > 0.0, max_local / np.maximum(colored, 1.0), 0.0)

    # globally largest colour class (uses color_sizes, which the policy currently ignores)
    big = int(np.argmax(color_sizes)) if color_sizes.size > 0 else 0
    touch_big = nc[:, big] / np.maximum(degree.astype(float), 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([concentration, touch_big])

features.name: second_order_saturation_peak_and_density
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, fraction of neighbours still uncoloured, the highest colour-saturation among its uncoloured neighbours (peak pressure), and the degree-normalised average saturation of those neighbours (density pressure)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 4))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    cmax = max(c, 1)

    # first-order saturation: distinct colours already sitting on its neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / cmax

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    # peak second-order pressure: the most saturated uncoloured neighbour
    masked = np.where(adjacency, sat[None, :], -1.0)
    peak = masked.max(axis=1)
    has_nb = adjacency.any(axis=1)
    peak = np.where(has_nb, np.maximum(peak, 0.0), 0.0) / cmax

    # density second-order pressure: saturation per unit of the neighbour's own
    # remaining freedom -- a low-degree, highly saturated neighbour is a bottleneck
    nb_weight = sat / (uncol + 1.0)                   # (k,) per-candidate pressure
    density = (adjf @ nb_weight) / np.maximum(uncol, 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, peak, density])
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, fraction of neighbours still uncoloured, the highest colour-saturation among its uncoloured neighbours (peak pressure), and the degree-normalised average saturation of those neighbours (density pressure).

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, fraction of its neighbours still uncoloured, and saturation-weighted contention for the colour it would itself take (neighbours with few free colours count more)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)

    # first-order saturation
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / max(c, 1)

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    # the colour this candidate would take: first zero column, else a new colour c
    avail = neighbor_colors == 0
    if c == 0:
        first = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.intp)
        avail_full = np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)
    else:
        any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
        avail_full = np.concatenate([avail, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)

    # how many colours each vertex still has left: free used colours + always-available new colour
    free_cols = (c - sat) + 1.0                      # >= 1
    w = 1.0 / free_cols                              # nearly-forced neighbours weigh most

    # can neighbour j still take the colour candidate i would take?
    lose = avail_full[:, first].T.astype(float)      # (k, k): [i, j]
    pressure = ((adjf * lose) * w[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    pressure_frac = pressure / np.maximum(uncol + 1.0, 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, pressure_frac])

features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: (1) mean colour-saturation of its uncoloured neighbours, (2) scarcity-weighted share of used colours reachable within two uncoloured hops, (3) fraction of its distance-two uncoloured vertices that already have its own first-fit colour sitting on a coloured neighbour (pre-blocked target colour)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0 or c == 0:
        return np.zeros((k, 3))

    present = neighbor_colors > 0                       # (k, c) bool
    sat = present.sum(axis=1).astype(float)             # (k,)
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol_deg = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    inv_deg = 1.0 / np.maximum(uncol_deg, 1.0)

    # (1) smoothed DSATUR: how constrained are the uncoloured vertices around me
    col1 = np.clip((adjf @ sat) * inv_deg / c, 0.0, 1.0)

    # (2) colours visible at distance <= 2, weighted by how rare (expensive) the
    # colour class is -- losing a scarce colour matters more than a fat one
    size = np.maximum(color_sizes.astype(float), 1.0)
    scarce = 1.0 / size                                 # (c,)
    twohop_present = (adjf @ present.astype(float)) > 0
    reach_mask = present | twohop_present               # (k, c) bool
    col2 = np.clip((reach_mask.astype(float) @ scarce) / max(scarce.sum(), 1e-12), 0.0, 1.0)

    # uncoloured distance-two mask
    eye = np.eye(k, dtype=bool)
    a2 = (adjf @ adjf) > 0
    a2 &= ~adjacency
    a2 &= ~eye
    d2 = a2.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    # (3) the colour this candidate would take
    avail = ~present
    any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
    first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
    safe_first = np.minimum(first, c - 1)
    T = present[:, safe_first].astype(float)            # T[j, i]: j already sees colour first[i]
    T[:, first >= c] = 0.0                              # a brand-new colour is not blocked anywhere
    pressure = np.diag(a2.astype(float) @ T)            # distance-2 vertices pre-touching my target colour
    col3 = np.clip(pressure / np.maximum(d2, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([col1, col2, col3])
features.measures: Per candidate: (1) mean colour-saturation of its uncoloured neighbours, (2) scarcity-weighted share of used colours reachable within two uncoloured hops, (3) fraction of its distance-two uncoloured vertices that already have its own first-fit colour sitting on a coloured neighbour (pre-blocked target colour).

features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: how much smaller its uncoloured degree is than its uncoloured neighbours' (relative-degeneracy), how tightly its uncoloured neighbours are interconnected (local cohesion), and the fraction of them that are near-leaves (only it as an uncoloured neighbour)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0) if k else 1.0

    # uncoloured degree of each candidate and the mean uncoloured degree of its
    # uncoloured neighbours: a vertex that is locally low-degree is a degeneracy
    # "peeler" and should be coloured early; a local hub later.
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    nb_deg = (adjf @ uncol) / np.maximum(uncol, 1.0)
    rel_degeneracy = np.clip((uncol - nb_deg) / dmax, -1.0, 1.0)

    # local cohesion: share of pairs of its uncoloured neighbours that are joined
    # (triangles through the candidate). Dense local clusters spread constraints.
    tri2 = (adjf @ adjf * adjf).sum(axis=1)          # = 2 * triangles at i
    pairs = np.maximum(uncol * (uncol - 1.0), 1.0)
    cohesion = np.clip(tri2 / pairs, 0.0, 1.0)

    # near-leaf attachment: fraction of its uncoloured neighbours that have at
    # most one uncoloured neighbour left (i.e. hang off the rest of the subgraph).
    near_leaf = (uncol <= 1.0).astype(float)
    leaf_frac = np.clip((adjf @ near_leaf) / np.maximum(uncol, 1.0), 0.0, 1.0)

    out = np.column_stack([rel_degeneracy, cohesion, leaf_frac])
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=-1.0)
features.measures: Per candidate: how much smaller its uncoloured degree is than its uncoloured neighbours' (relative-degeneracy), how tightly its uncoloured neighbours are interconnected (local cohesion), and the fraction of them that are near-leaves (only it as an uncoloured neighbour).

features.code:
import numpy as np


def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: how big its first-fit colour class would become if it were coloured now (existing members plus uncoloured non-neighbours that can still take that colour), as a fraction of the graph, and the share of its uncoloured non-neighbours already blocked from that colour."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))

    # the colour each candidate would take: first zero column, else a new colour c
    avail = neighbor_colors == 0
    if c == 0:
        first = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.intp)
        avail_full = np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)
    else:
        any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
        avail_full = np.concatenate([avail, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)

    # free[j, i] = True when candidate j could still take the colour first[i]
    free = avail_full[:, first]                       # (k, k), row j, col i

    nonnbr = ~adjacency
    np.fill_diagonal(nonnbr, False)

    # uncoloured non-neighbours that could join the class (growth headroom)
    grow = (nonnbr & free).sum(axis=0).astype(float)
    # uncoloured non-neighbours already blocked from that colour
    blocked = (nonnbr & ~free).sum(axis=0).astype(float)

    # size the colour class already has (0 for a brand-new colour)
    sz = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)
    if c > 0:
        mask = first < c
        if mask.any():
            sz[mask] = color_sizes[first[mask]].astype(float)

    n = float(k + int(color_sizes.sum()))
    if n < 1.0:
        n = 1.0

    class_fill = (sz + grow) / n
    blocked_share = blocked / n

    return np.column_stack([class_fill, blocked_share])
features.measures: Per candidate: how big its first-fit colour class would become if it were coloured now (existing members plus uncoloured non-neighbours that can still take that colour), as a fraction of the graph, and the share of its uncoloured non-neighbours already blocked from that colour.

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: saturation share, share of its uncoloured neighbours that could still take the candidate's own target colour, and the share of those neighbours that are one colour away from being forced to open a new class."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)

    # saturation share: distinct colours already touching the candidate
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / max(c, 1)

    # remaining (uncoloured) neighbourhood size
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_safe = np.maximum(uncol, 1.0)

    # the colour this candidate would take: first zero column, else a new colour c
    avail = neighbor_colors == 0                      # (k, c)
    if c == 0:
        first = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.intp)
        avail_full = np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)
        free = np.ones(k, dtype=float)                # only "new colour" is available
    else:
        any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
        avail_full = np.concatenate([avail, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)
        free = avail.sum(axis=1).astype(float) + 1.0  # free existing + possible new colour

    # lose[i, j] = True if the colour candidate i would take is still free for candidate j
    lose = avail_full[:, first].T.astype(float)
    impact = (adjf * lose).sum(axis=1)
    # NEW normalisation: blocking expressed as a SHARE of the remaining neighbours, not a count
    impact_share = impact / uncol_safe

    # NEW quantity: uncoloured neighbours that are already down to a single option
    # (no free existing colour, so only a brand new class remains for them)
    tight = (free <= 1.0).astype(float)
    nb_tight_share = (adjf @ tight) / uncol_safe

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, impact_share, nb_tight_share])
features.measures: Per candidate: saturation share, share of its uncoloured neighbours that could still take the candidate's own target colour, and the share of those neighbours that are one colour away from being forced to open a new class.

features.code:
import numpy as np


def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: share of its uncoloured neighbours that would first-fit to the same colour, and share of uncoloured vertices it is adjacent to."""
    neighbor_colors = np.asarray(neighbor_colors)
    adjacency = np.asarray(adjacency)
    k = adjacency.shape[0]
    neighbor_colors = neighbor_colors.reshape(k, -1)
    c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]

    if c == 0:
        ff = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.int64)
    else:
        free = (neighbor_colors == 0)
        has_free = free.any(axis=1)
        ff = np.argmax(free, axis=1).astype(np.int64)
        ff = np.where(has_free, ff, c).astype(np.int64)

    same = (ff[:, None] == ff[None, :])
    same &= ~np.eye(k, dtype=bool)
    mates = same.sum(axis=1).astype(float).reshape(k)

    links = np.asarray(adjacency.astype(float) @ same.astype(float)).reshape(k)
    conflict_share = links / np.maximum(mates, 1.0)

    adj_deg = np.asarray(adjacency.sum(axis=1)).astype(float).reshape(k)
    uncoloured_degree_share = adj_deg / max(k - 1, 1)

    return np.stack([conflict_share.reshape(k),
                     uncoloured_degree_share.reshape(k)], axis=1)

idea.hypothesis: Planted fails by class contamination: the first-fit colour of a candidate (the first colour it is not adjacent to) defines the class it joins, but two candidates targeting the same colour may be adjacent to each other, so colouring one now evicts the other and the class fragments into many medium classes (smallest_class 6 vs ref 16, 10 colours vs 6). RLF forbids exactly this: within the set of candidates that would take the same colour, pick the one adjacent to the fewest of them, so the class can still absorb the rest. Column 1 is that conflict share, column 2 is the remaining (uncoloured) degree share.
idea.feature: Two columns. Column 1: compute the first-fit colour ff of each candidate (`free = (neighbor_colors == 0)`; `ff = first True index of free per row`, or `c` if the row has no zero = forced opener; if c == 0 set ff = 0 for all). Build `same = (ff[:,None] == ff[None,:])` with the diagonal set False, `mates = same.sum(axis=1)`, `links = adjacency.astype(float) @ same.astype(float)`, column 1 = `links / max(mates, 1)`. Column 2: `adjacency.sum(axis=1) / max(k-1, 1)`. Return stacked (k, 2).
idea.lesson: f015 measured only how many candidates shared the target colour and its planted prediction (colors 10 -> 11) failed: class size alone is not the mechanism. The missing ingredient is which of those co-targeters are adjacent to the candidate, i.e. how many the move evicts.

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of its uncoloured neighbours that its first-fit colour would push from two free colours down to one."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)
    if c == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    is_zero = (neighbor_colors == 0)                 # (k, c): colour still free for this candidate
    has_zero = is_zero.any(axis=1)
    ff = np.where(has_zero, np.argmax(is_zero, axis=1), c)   # first zero column, else c

    F = c - (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1)        # free colours remaining per candidate
    valid = (is_zero & (F[:, None] == 2)).astype(float)      # (k, c)

    # W[u, v] = valid[u, ff[v]]; pad a zero column for ff[v] == c (opens a new colour, destroys nothing)
    valid_ext = np.concatenate([valid, np.zeros((k, 1))], axis=1)
    W = valid_ext[:, ff]                             # (k, k)

    score = (adjacency.astype(float) * W).sum(axis=0) / np.maximum(adjacency.sum(axis=1), 1)
    return score

Colouring candidate v with its first-fit colour j removes j from every neighbour u with j still free for it. Measuring that dilation (neighbours with F==2 and j free) is a softer, higher-signal lookahead and predicts where the extra colours come from.
idea.feature: One column. If c == 0 return zeros(k). Else: ff = first zero column of neighbor_colors per row (else c); F = c - (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1); build `valid[u, j] = 1.0 if neighbor_colors[u, j] == 0 and F[u] == 2 else 0` (shape (k, c)); `W = valid[:, ff]` (k x k, W[u, v] = valid[u, ff[v]]); score = `(adjacency.astype(float) * W).sum(axis=0)` divided by `max(adjacency.sum(axis=1), 1)`. features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, fraction of its neighbours still uncoloured, and the uncoloured-degree-weighted average colour-saturation of its uncoloured neighbours (hub-favouring second-order pressure)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    cmax = max(c, 1)

    # first-order saturation: how many distinct colours already sit on its neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / cmax

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    # second-order pressure, but each uncoloured neighbour's saturation is weighted
    # by *that neighbour's* own uncoloured degree: a constrained hub neighbour
    # matters more than a constrained leaf, so a vertex sitting next to hubs that
    # are themselves getting boxed in should be coloured before its own first-order
    # saturation catches up.
    nb_total_w = adjf @ uncol                      # sum of neighbour uncoloured degrees
    nb_weighted_sat = adjf @ (sat * uncol)         # degree-weighted neighbour saturation
    nb_hub_sat_frac = nb_weighted_sat / np.maximum(nb_total_w * cmax, 1.0)

    out = np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, np.nan_to_num(nb_hub_sat_frac, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)])
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, fraction of its neighbours still uncoloured, and the uncoloured-degree-weighted average colour-saturation of its uncoloured neighbours (hub-favouring second-order pressure).

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours already touching it, the share of its own degree that is still uncoloured, and (over its free colours) the smallest number of uncoloured neighbours that could also take that colour, as a share of its uncoloured neighbours."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))

    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)                      # uncoloured neighbours (remaining degree)
    deg = np.maximum(degree.astype(float), 1.0)

    # 1) first-order saturation: distinct used colours on its neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / max(c, 1)

    # 2) relative remaining freedom: what share of its OWN degree is still uncoloured
    #    (per-candidate normalisation, not a global max-degree normalisation)
    uncol_frac = uncol / deg

    # 3) flexibility of colour choice: for every colour still free at this candidate,
    #    count the uncoloured neighbours that could also take it; take the minimum
    #    (the least contested free colour) as a share of its uncoloured neighbours.
    if c == 0:
        contention = np.ones(k)                   # no colours yet: everyone opens a new class
    else:
        avail = (neighbor_colors == 0).astype(float)   # (k, c) colours still free here
        contention_mat = adjf @ avail                  # (k, c) neighbours that share each colour
        blocked = np.where(avail > 0, contention_mat, np.inf)
        min_cont = blocked.min(axis=1)
        has_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        # no free colour -> must open a new class: maximal contention
        min_cont = np.where(has_free, min_cont, uncol)
        contention = min_cont / np.maximum(uncol, 1.0)

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, contention])
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours already touching it, the share of its own degree that is still uncoloured, and (over its free colours) the smallest number of uncoloured neighbours that could also take that colour, as a share of its uncoloured neighbours.

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Fill pressure for the *smallest* existing colour class a candidate can still take (new colour penalised), crossed with the candidate's uncoloured-degree and saturation, so class-filling is conditioned on local structure."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 3))

    n = k + float(color_sizes.sum())
    if n <= 0.0:
        return np.zeros((k, 3))

    # local uncoloured structure of each candidate
    uncol = adjacency.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    uncol_frac = uncol / max(1.0, float(degree.max()))
    sat_frac = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float) / max(c, 1)

    if c == 0:
        # no colours yet: every candidate would open colour 0
        fill = np.full(k, -1.0 / n, dtype=float)
    else:
        free = neighbor_colors == 0                      # (k, c)
        has_free = free.any(axis=1)
        big = n + 1.0
        masked = np.where(free, color_sizes[None, :].astype(float), big)
        # smallest existing class still open to this candidate
        min_avail = masked.min(axis=1)
        # good: join a small existing class; bad: force a brand-new colour
        fill = np.where(has_free, -(min_avail + 1.0) / n, -1.0)
        fill = fill.astype(float)

    return np.column_stack([fill, fill * uncol_frac, fill * sat_frac])
features.measures: Fill pressure for the *smallest* existing colour class a candidate can still take (new colour penalised), crossed with the candidate's uncoloured-degree and saturation, so class-filling is conditioned on local structure.

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: among its uncoloured neighbours that could also still take the candidate's first-fit colour, the fraction that are mutually non-adjacent (i.e. colour-sharing opportunities its colouring would waste)."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros(0)

    # colour the candidate would first-fit into (new colour c if none is free)
    avail = neighbor_colors == 0                      # (k, c)
    if c > 0:
        any_free = avail.any(axis=1)
        first = np.where(any_free, avail.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.intp)
    else:
        first = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.intp)
    avail_full = np.concatenate([avail, np.ones((k, 1), dtype=bool)], axis=1)

    # B[j, i] = 1 iff j is an uncoloured neighbour of i and j is still free for i's first-fit colour
    B = adjacency.astype(float) * avail_full[:, first]        # (k, k)

    # W = non-adjacency among uncoloured vertices (sharing the colour would be useful there)
    W = (~adjacency).astype(float)
    np.fill_diagonal(W, 0.0)

    # ordered non-adjacent pairs inside each candidate's blocked set
    Q = B.T @ W @ B
    harm = 0.5 * np.diag(Q)

    uncol = adjacency.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    denom = np.maximum(uncol * (uncol - 1.0) * 0.5, 1.0)
    return np.clip(harm / denom, 0.0, 1.0)
features.measures: Per candidate: among its uncoloured neighbours that could also still take the candidate's first-fit colour, the fraction that are mutually non-adjacent (i.e. colour-sharing opportunities its colouring would waste).

import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: edge density among its still-uncoloured neighbours (triangle density through the vertex) and the mean uncoloured degree of those neighbours relative to the max degree."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 2))

    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)

    # triangles through each vertex in the uncoloured subgraph:
    # (A^2)[i, j] counts common uncoloured neighbours of i and j;
    # 0.5 * sum_j A[i, j] * A^2[i, j] = number of triangles at i.
    a2 = adjf @ adjf
    tri = 0.5 * (adjf * a2).sum(axis=1)

    # density of the candidate's uncoloured neighbourhood (0 when < 2 neighbours)
    pairs = uncol * (uncol - 1.0) * 0.5
    tri_density = np.where(uncol >= 2.0, tri / np.maximum(pairs, 1.0), 0.0)

    # second-order structural degree: how dense the neighbourhood of the
    # candidate's uncoloured neighbours is on average
    nb_deg = adjf @ uncol
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    nb_deg_frac = nb_deg / np.maximum(uncol * dmax, 1.0)

    out = np.column_stack([tri_density, nb_deg_frac])
    return np.nan_to_num(out, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=0.0)
features.measures: Per candidate: edge density among its still-uncoloured neighbours (triangle density through the vertex) and the mean uncoloured degree of those neighbours relative to the max degree.

features.name: peak_and_blocked_second_order_saturation
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, its fraction of uncoloured neighbours, the PEAK (not mean) colour-saturation among its uncoloured neighbours, and the fraction of those uncoloured neighbours that are already fully blocked from every used colour."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if k == 0:
        return np.zeros((0, 4))
    dmax = max(float(degree.max()), 1.0)
    cmax = max(c, 1)

    # first-order saturation: distinct used colours sitting on the candidate's neighbours
    sat = (neighbor_colors > 0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    sat_frac = sat / cmax

    # remaining (uncoloured) degree
    adjf = adjacency.astype(float)
    uncol = adjf.sum(axis=1)
    uncol_frac = uncol / dmax

    if c > 0:
        # peak second-order pressure: the single most constrained uncoloured neighbour
        # (bold change: max instead of mean -> a different ordering of candidates)
        sat_mat = np.where(adjacency, sat[None, :], -1.0)
        peak = sat_mat.max(axis=1)
        peak = np.where(uncol > 0.0, peak, 0.0)
        peak_frac = peak / cmax

        # trapped neighbours: how many uncoloured neighbours have no free used colour left
        blocked = np.where(adjacency, (sat[None, :] >= c).astype(float), 0.0).sum(axis=1)
        blocked_frac = blocked / np.maximum(uncol, 1.0)
    else:
        peak_frac = np.zeros(k)
        blocked_frac = np.zeros(k)

    return np.column_stack([sat_frac, uncol_frac, peak_frac, blocked_frac])
features.measures: Per candidate: fraction of used colours touching it, its fraction of uncoloured neighbours, the PEAK (not mean) colour-saturation among its uncoloured neighbours, and the fraction of those uncoloured neighbours that are already fully blocked from every used colour.

features.name: lowest_firstfit_class_order
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: negative first-fit colour class (higher = lower open class), and share of remaining vertices that are its neighbours."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    if c == 0:
        ff = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
        deg_rem = degree.astype(np.float64)
    else:
        free = (neighbor_colors == 0)
        has_free = free.any(axis=1)
        ff = np.where(has_free, free.argmax(axis=1), c).astype(np.float64)
        # uncoloured neighbours = total degree - coloured neighbours
        deg_rem = degree.astype(np.float64) - neighbor_colors.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
    col1 = -ff / float(c + 1)
    col2 = deg_rem / float(max(k - 1, 1))
    return np.column_stack([col1, col2])

idea.hypothesis: The champion's order jumps between colour classes, so planted (10 colours vs 6, last colour opened at 92% of the order) and dense (13 vs 11, last at 90%) keep opening classes near the end. If the ordering variable is which class is being filled rather than the saturation count, preferring the candidate whose first-fit colour is the lowest open class, tie-broken by uncoloured degree, fills class 0 to a maximal independent set before class 1 opens and removes those late extra classes.
idea.feature: Two columns (k candidates, c = neighbor_colors.shape[1]). ff[i] = smallest column j with neighbor_colors[i,j]==0; if c==0 then ff[i]=0 for all i; if no column is free then ff[i]=c. col1 = -ff/(c+1) (higher = lower open class). col2 = adjacency.sum(axis=1)/max(k-1,1) (share of remaining vertices that are the candidate's neighbours). Return np.column_stack([col1, col2]).
idea.lesson: f015 weighted the first-fit class size on top of saturation and planted went 10 -> 11; the class index itself has never been the ordering variable.

features.coder_note: It computes, for each candidate, the negated first-fit colour index (divided by c+1, so lower open classes score higher), and the fraction of the other uncoloured vertices it is adjacent to; I read "uncoloured degree" per the formula given as `adjacency.sum(axis=1)/(k-1)`, and treat `c==0` as ff=0 …
features.measures: Per candidate: negative first-fit colour class (higher = lower open class), and share of remaining vertices that are its neighbours.

features.name: rlf_pool_and_forbidden_links
features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(neighbor_colors, adjacency, degree, color_sizes):
    """Per candidate: its first-fit colour's available-neighbour pool size and forbidden-link count, each divided by k-1."""
    k, c = neighbor_colors.shape
    denom = max(k - 1, 1)

    if c == 0:
        return np.column_stack([
            adjacency.sum(1).astype(float) / denom,
            np.zeros(k, dtype=float),
        ])

    zero = (neighbor_colors == 0)
    any_av = zero.any(1)
    ff = np.where(any_av, np.argmax(zero, 1), c)

    ind = zero[:, np.minimum(ff, c - 1)].astype(float)
    ind[:, ~any_av] = 1.0

    pool = (adjacency.astype(float) * ind.T).sum(1)
    forbidden = adjacency.sum(1).astype(float) - pool

    return np.column_stack([pool, forbidden]) / denom

idea.hypothesis: RLF builds each class as a near-independent set: inside the current class pick the vertex with the largest degree in the pool of vertices that can still share its colour and the fewest links to vertices already excluded from it. The champion has no term for whether a candidate's neighbourhood can still share its colour, so classes come out ragged (dense smallest class 4 vs 5, planted 10 colours vs 6). If class coherence is the missing variable, this cuts colours on dense and planted.
idea.feature: Two columns. zero = (neighbor_colors == 0). If c == 0: return np.column_stack([adjacency.sum(1)/max(k-1,1), np.zeros(k)]). Else any_av = zero.any(1); ff = np.where(any_av, np.argmax(zero, 1), c); ind = zero[:, np.minimum(ff, c-1)].astype(float) so ind[j,i] = vertex j can still take candidate i's first-fit colour; ind[:, ~any_av] = 1.0 (a new-colour opener's pool is every uncoloured vertex); pool = (adjacency.astype(float) * ind.T).sum(1); forbidden = adjacency.sum(1) - pool; return np.column_stack([pool, forbidden]) / max(k-1, 1).
idea.lesson: f024 (rlf_class_conflict_ratio) was invalid on a shape error, so RLF class building has never actually been evaluated.

features.coder_note: This computes, for each candidate, how many uncoloured neighbours could still take its first-fit colour (the pool) and how many cannot (forbidden links), both normalised by the number of other candidates; when no colours are used yet it returns normalised degree as the pool and zero forbidden links.
features.measures: Per candidate: its first-fit colour's available-neighbour pool size and forbidden-link count, each divided by k-1.

prediction.why: not checked: the feature made the policy much worse at every weight tried

features.name: demand_weighted_blocking_and_target_pool

idea.hypothesis: Counting blocked colours equally treats a colour nearly every remaining vertex can take the same as one with two takers left. Weighting each blocked colour by its remaining demand, with the plain count subtracted (it is already in f005), isolates the demand signal: if demand matters, the policy stops spending the last takers of a colour, and dense's 12th/13th colours (smallest class 4 vs 5, last colour at 90% of the order) disappear.
idea.feature: Two columns. zero = (neighbor_colors == 0); demand_frac = zero.sum(0)/k (share of uncoloured vertices that can still take each colour); mean_d = demand_frac.mean() if c > 0 else 0.0; col1 = ((neighbor_colors > 0) * (demand_frac - mean_d)[None, :]).sum(1)/max(c, 1) (blocked colours weighted by demand with the equal-count component removed); ff = np.argmax(zero, 1) where zero.any(1) else c (all 0 when c == 0); col2 = demand_frac[np.minimum(ff, c-1)] for ff < c, else 1.0 (a new colour's demand is every remaining vertex); return np.column_stack([col1, col2]).
idea.lesson: f015 targeted class size and failed (planted 10 -> 11) and f002's scarcity column was redundant; this tests demand (who can still use a colour), orthogonalised against the plain blocked-colour count f005 already carries.

features.coder_note: The code computes the demand-weighted blocked-colour score with the equal-count component removed as column 1, and the remaining demand share of the candidate’s first takeable colour (or 1.0 for opening a new colour) as column 2; when no colour exists yet, column 1 is 0 and column 2 is 1.0.
features.measures: Per candidate: blocked colours weighted by remaining demand minus the plain count, and the demand of the colour the candidate would take (new colour demand = 1).

prediction.why: inert at the fitted weight and at an exaggerated one: the metric didn't move, so not checked

nodes.title: Saturation degree (DSATUR)

nodes.title: One-step impact / lookahead
